introduction: On this third Sunday of Easter, the two disciples from Emmaus tell how they recognized Jesus in the breaking of the bread, and then he stands among the apostles. He shows them his hands and feet, eats with them and opens their minds to understand the Scriptures. Peter calls the people to repentance, and John reminds us that Jesus is our advocate with the Father. Let us recognize the risen Lord in his word and at this table.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the risen Lord opens our minds to understand the Scriptures. Let us bring our prayers to the Father.
intentions: For the Church: that she may proclaim repentance and forgiveness in the name of Jesus to all the nations. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who preach and teach the faith: that their words may set hearts burning with the love of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are frightened or troubled: that the risen Lord may stand among them and give them his peace. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have turned away from God: that they may hear the call to turn back and find their sins forgiven. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may recognize Jesus in the breaking of the bread and in the reading of the Scriptures. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God of life, your Son showed himself alive to his disciples and opened the Scriptures to them. Open our minds and hearts to know him, and send us out as his witnesses. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: You are witnesses
reflection.body:
The two disciples have just come back from Emmaus. They tell the others how Jesus walked with them, and "how he was recognized by them in the breaking of the bread." While they are still talking, Jesus himself stands among them.

The disciples are terrified; they think they are seeing a ghost. Jesus is patient with them. "Why are you troubled? Why do doubts arise in your hearts? See my hands and my feet, that it is truly me." Then he asks for something to eat, and eats a piece of fish in front of them. The risen Jesus is not a memory or an idea. He is the same Lord, with a real body, now glorified.

Then "he opened their minds, that they might understand the Scriptures." He shows them that everything written about him "in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms" had to be fulfilled. And he gives them their mission: repentance and the forgiveness of sins are to be preached in his name to all nations. "You are witnesses of these things."

Peter takes up that mission in the first reading. He speaks plainly to the crowd about the death of Jesus, but he does not crush them. "I know that you did this in ignorance," he says, and he invites them: "Repent therefore, and turn again, that your sins may be blotted out." John says the same with great tenderness: "If anyone sins, we have a Counselor with the Father, Jesus Christ, the righteous."

Every Sunday follows the same pattern as that evening in Jerusalem: Jesus opens the Scriptures to us, and he gives himself in the breaking of the bread. This week, read the Gospel of next Sunday ahead of time, and ask the Lord to open your mind to it. Then, at Mass, watch for him at the altar.
